chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Imran al-Halbi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the person in Ihram who has a wound, so he treats it with a medication containing saffron. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the saffron is dominant in the medication, then (it is not permissible); and if the other medicines are dominant over it, then there is no problem.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in Ihram to use saffron-based medicine for a wound?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a nuanced legal principle for Ihram, distinguishing between the dominant nature of the substance and its medicinal utility to determine permissibility. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (rukhas) in ritual purity, ensuring that necessary medical treatments do not invalidate the state of consecration. It highlights the dynamic application of fiqh where the primary purpose of the item dictates its legal status rather than its mere presence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Imran Al Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the one in Ihraam who happens to be with an injury, so he treats with a medication which has saffron in it. Heasws said: ‘If it (saffron) was overwhelming upon the medication, so no; and if it was such that the medication was overwhelming upon it, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Imran al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram with a wound and treats it with a medicine which has saffron.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If saffron is overwhelming, it is not permissible; but if the medicine is overwhelming, it is not harmful.’”
